name: Wildschönau
kurzbeschreibung: The sunny high valley with the villages of Auffach, Oberau and Niederau – famous for Bregenzerwälder Käsknödel and a top ski paradise.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Wildschönau extends as a broad, sun-drenched high valley in the Kitzbühel Alps within the Tyrolean district of Kufstein. Branching south from the lower Inn Valley near Wörgl, the valley comprises four picturesque church villages: Niederau at 828 metres, Oberau as the administrative centre at 936 metres, Auffach at 875 metres, and idyllic Thierbach, which at 1,150 metres is the highest church village in the Kitzbühel Alps. Around 4,400 residents live in the valley, framed by alpine peaks such as the Großer Beil at 2,309 metres, Schatzberg at 1,903 metres, and Markbachjoch at 1,500 metres. Free from through traffic, Wildschönau preserves authentic mountain farming traditions and classic timber architecture.

Geschichte

Bavarian settlers began clearing the high valley around the year 1000. Wildschönau was first documented between 1193 and 1195 when Albert of Wildschönau witnessed a deed of donation by Count Heinrich of Lechsgemünd-Rettenberg. During the 15th and 16th centuries, silver and copper mining flourished, leaving historical tunnels near Thierbach. A unique historical tradition dates back to Empress Maria Theresa: around 1760, to support impoverished mountain farmers, she granted 51 farms an exclusive imperial monopoly to distill white stubble turnips into schnapps. This earthy turnip spirit, known as Krautinger, remains a protected cultural heritage. The parish church of St. Margaret in Oberau, known locally as the Cathedral of Wildschönau, was built in 1751 by master builder Franz de Paula Penz in elegant Rococo style.

Anreise

Reaching Wildschönau is straightforward thanks to its proximity to the Inn Valley. By car, travel along the Inntal motorway A12 to exit Wörgl Ost or Wörgl West, continuing up the well-maintained Wildschönauer Landesstraße L3 for about ten minutes to reach Niederau. Rail passengers arrive at Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, an international junction served by Railjet, ICE, and Eurocity trains. From the station square, regional bus line 4064 runs regularly into the valley serving Niederau, Oberau, and Auffach. Holidaymakers with the Wildschönau Card enjoy complimentary travel on all local hiking and ski buses throughout the valley.

Tipps

In winter, the Ski Juwel Alpbachtal Wildschönau ski area offers 113 kilometres of slopes and modern lifts connecting Schatzberg with Markbachjoch and the neighboring Alpbach valley. In summer, the Mountain Farming Museum z'Bach in Oberau, housed in a historic 1795 homestead, showcases rural tools and hosts traditional craft markets. The Kundler Klamm gorge offers an impressive walk along churning mountain waters towards Kundl, easily accessed via the nostalgic Wildschönau tourist train. In Auffach, the 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum presents intriguing wooden sculptures across 39 exhibition rooms, and sampling a glass of genuine Krautinger turnip schnapps is an essential cultural experience.
